title: Hibernation: keep native GPU drivers out of the initramfs so resume runs before any GPU driver touches the hardware
author: madakas
body:
## Problem

One mechanism sits behind #10061, #10039, #8352 and #7848: the initramfs loads the native GPU driver **before** the resume hook can run. The `kms` hook (or the NVIDIA `MODULES+=` drop-in, which busybox init modprobes before any hook) exists so Plymouth can theme the LUKS prompt — but the resume decision structurally cannot happen until *after* unlock, because the swapfile sits inside LUKS. So on every resume-from-hibernate boot, the boot kernel fully initializes the GPU, its `.freeze` callback then suspends **and ASIC-resets** it (amdgpu does this unconditionally on dGPUs since kernel commit `daf8de0874ab`), and the restored kernel has to reclaim hardware a second driver instance just reprogrammed. On robust hardware that survives; on plenty of real machines it does not — `nv_pmops_freeze → -EIO` on NVIDIA, nouveau FIFO faults on Macs, and a silent hard hang on amdgpu CIK iMacs (silent because the whole window runs with consoles suspended and Arch builds without `CONFIG_DPM_WATCHDOG`). Full source-level analysis with citations: https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/issues/10061#issuecomment-5532141219

Two reporters have already verified the workaround independently (#10039, #8352): remove the GPU driver from the initramfs and resume works. Fedora shipped exactly this model distro-wide in F42 ([Changes/PlymouthUseSimpledrm](https://fedoraproject.org/wiki/Changes/PlymouthUseSimpledrm)).

## Fix

Hibernation-scoped, so nobody else's boot experience changes: while hibernation is configured, keep native GPU drivers out of the initramfs and let Plymouth render the LUKS prompt on simpledrm (EFI framebuffer, native resolution).

- `omarchy-hibernation-setup` now writes a drop-in that adds the `resume` hook, **strips `kms`**, and filters the NVIDIA early-KMS modules out of `MODULES` (dead weight otherwise — the blacklist guarantees they never load); installs a new self-contained `omarchy-defer-gpu` initcpio hook that bakes an **initramfs-only** modprobe blacklist into the image (never into host `/etc/modprobe.d`, which `modconf` would copy in and which would affect the running system); and appends `plymouth.use-simpledrm` to the cmdline drop-in, which it now rewrites on every run so a pre-existing file can't pin a stale resume offset. The blacklist also covers the NVIDIA `MODULES+=` early load (`modprobe -qab`'s `-b` applies blacklists to explicit names), so `install/hardware/nvidia.sh` only gains a cross-reference comment. Setup also upgrades old-format installs in place — an existing resume drop-in without the defer-gpu hook reruns the idempotent setup instead of early-exiting, so current hibernation users receive the fix — and aborts cleanly before touching initramfs config if the resume offset can't be determined.
- `omarchy-hibernation-remove` now deletes everything setup created — including the `resume.conf` and `rtc-alarm.conf` limine-entry-tool drop-ins, *before* the rebuild. Fixes #10037 (removal used to leave `resume=` pointing at the deleted swapfile in every regenerated boot entry).
- On normal boots the real root's udev loads the GPU driver right after `switch_root` (one brief modeset handoff — the trade-off Fedora accepted). On resume boots the restored kernel reclaims the GPU from clean, EFI-posted state — the path its S4 restore code is actually written for.

## Testing

On the affected hardware class (iMac17,1, amdgpu Bonaire/CIK, Btrfs+LUKS, Limine/UKI, the machine from #10061):

- `bash -n` on both scripts; drop-in logic unit-tested in isolation (kms stripped, resume + omarchy-defer-gpu appended, MODULES untouched).
- Built a real initramfs with the resulting config (`mkinitcpio -D` with the new hook): **zero** GPU modules in the image (production image on the same machine carries amdgpu), blacklist present at `etc/modprobe.d/99-omarchy-defer-gpu.conf`, `hooks/resume` + `systemd-hibernate-resume` + Plymouth all present. Side effect: image size dropped 61 MB → 24 MB.
- Not yet tested: an actual hibernate/resume cycle with this config on the CIK iMac — that machine currently has hibernation disabled after the incident in #10061. Happy to be the guinea pig once this lands in a testable state, ideally paired with the `resume=`-free rescue boot entry proposed in #10061 as the safety net.

## Open questions for maintainers

- Existing hibernation users get upgraded when they next run `omarchy hibernation setup` (old-format drop-ins are detected and rewritten in place). If you'd rather push the upgrade proactively, a `migrations/` script can call the same idempotent path — happy to add it.
- Fedora documented two edge cases that may eventually want an opt-out: docks where the only monitor hangs off a secondary GPU (dark LUKS prompt), and rare AMD laptops needing amdgpu firmware in the initrd for USB-C boot.
- The kms-strip logic lives in the setup-written drop-in; an alternative is centralizing kms policy in the pacman-owned `omarchy_hooks.conf` (checking for the resume drop-in's existence). Kept scoped here to avoid touching the always-installed file — your call.
- The bolder version of this change is Fedora's: drop `kms` from the initramfs unconditionally (smaller images, faster boots, deletes the NVIDIA kms-drop special case in `omarchy_hooks.conf`). This PR deliberately stays scoped to hibernation.

P.S. Greetings to @dhh from Max — Omarchy brought this 2015 iMac gloriously back to life; this PR is for the one button that tried to take it back down. ;-)

+sudo tee "$MKINITCPIO_CONF" >/dev/null <<'EOF'
+HOOKS+=(resume omarchy-defer-gpu)
+
+# Early KMS is incompatible with resume-from-hibernate: the kms hook puts the
+# native GPU driver in the initramfs, udev coldplug binds it before the resume
+# hook can run, and the restored kernel then has to reclaim hardware a second
+# driver instance suspended and reset. Strip kms while hibernation is
+# configured; Plymouth uses simpledrm for the LUKS prompt instead.

+for _omarchy_hook in "${HOOKS[@]}"; do
+  [[ $_omarchy_hook == "kms" ]] || _omarchy_hooks+=("$_omarchy_hook")

+  esac
+done
+MODULES=("${_omarchy_modules[@]}")
+unset _omarchy_modules _omarchy_module
+EOF

+#!/bin/bash
+
+build() {
+  local conf
+  conf=$(mktemp)
+  cat > "$conf" <<'EOF'
+# Initramfs-only: keep native GPU drivers out of early boot while hibernation
+# is configured. A driver bound by the boot kernel before the resume hook
+# fires suspends and resets hardware the restored kernel cannot reclaim,
+# which hangs or faults resume-from-hibernate (amdgpu CIK, NVIDIA, nouveau).
+# Deferral is deliberately uniform across vendors: driver-vs-driver hardware
+# reclaim is not vendor-specific and multi-GPU detection is fragile, so every
+# hibernation system trades early KMS for a simpledrm LUKS prompt.
+#
+# blacklist also covers the explicit MODULES=() load: mkinitcpio's init uses
+# modprobe -qab, and -b applies blacklists to explicit names too.
+# Keep the nvidia list in sync with install/hardware/nvidia.sh.
+blacklist amdgpu
+blacklist radeon
+blacklist nouveau
+blacklist nvidia
+blacklist nvidia_drm
+blacklist nvidia_modeset
+blacklist nvidia_uvm
+blacklist i915
+blacklist xe
+EOF
+  add_file "$conf" /etc/modprobe.d/99-omarchy-defer-gpu.conf 644
+  rm -f "$conf"
+}
+
+help() {
+  cat <<HELPEOF
+Bakes an initramfs-only modprobe blacklist into the image that keeps native
+GPU drivers out of early boot while hibernation is configured, so the resume
+hook runs before any GPU driver touches the hardware. Self-contained: the
+blacklist never exists on the host filesystem, where modconf would copy it in
+and where it would also affect the running system. Installed to
+/etc/initcpio/install by omarchy-hibernation-setup and removed by
+omarchy-hibernation-remove.
+HELPEOF
+}

@@ -25,7 +25,10 @@ if lspci | grep -qi 'nvidia'; then
 options nvidia_drm modeset=1
 EOF
 
-  # Configure mkinitcpio for early loading

+  # with the blacklist and MODULES filter in
+  # default/initcpio/install/omarchy-defer-gpu and omarchy-hibernation-setup:
+  # hibernation defers exactly these modules out of the initramfs.
   mkdir -p /etc/mkinitcpio.conf.d
   cat > /etc/mkinitcpio.conf.d/nvidia.conf <<'EOF'
 MODULES+=(nvidia nvidia_modeset nvidia_uvm nvidia_drm)
